description: Uncover the market, river crossing and priory that shaped St Neots before finishing where the town’s old coaching story is remembered.
author: Day Tripping Quiz

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A priory’s weekly market grew into the broad civic heart of this river town.
stops.Hint_1: Begin in the large open square at the centre of St Neots.
stops.Hint_2: Stand where the regular town market is held, surrounded by historic frontages.
stops.Unlock_Fact: St Neots developed around its priory and river crossing. A weekly Thursday market was authorised by 1130, bringing trade and income to the monks and helping the settlement grow.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Choose one historic-looking frontage around the square and note its roofline or building material.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Monks, merchants and modern traffic have all crossed the Ouse here, but today’s bridge is not the old stone span.
stops.Hint_1: Walk west from Market Square towards the River Great Ouse.
stops.Hint_2: Find the present road bridge and view it from a safe public pavement.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The river crossing helped make St Neots a market town. A stone bridge built around 1617 survived until 1964, when it was demolished and replaced by the present concrete crossing.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the pavement, notice one clearly modern material or shape in the present bridge.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: No monks chant here now, but this riverside centre keeps their vanished home in its name.
stops.Hint_1: Stay near the river and look for a modern community and events building.
stops.Hint_2: Find the Priory Centre beside the site of the medieval monastery.
stops.Unlock_Fact: A monastery was founded here around 974 and later rebuilt as a Benedictine priory. After the Dissolution its buildings disappeared; the site later became a brewery and now includes the Priory Centre.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look for the nearby surviving oast-house form or another exterior clue to the site’s later brewing history.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Return towards the market for a house named after the wheels and horses of the old north road.
stops.Hint_1: Walk back towards the High Street near Market Square.
stops.Hint_2: Find The Coach House at 18 High Street.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! St Neots grew as a river crossing and later prospered on busy coaching routes between London and the north. The Coach House’s name makes a fitting end to that travel story; stop for food or a drink if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, find one sign, doorway or courtyard feature that suits the coaching-house name.

short_description: A gentle Great Ouse circuit through markets, monks and changing bridges.

before_you_go.terrain: Level market-town pavements with short surfaced sections beside the Great Ouse and a riverside community area.
before_you_go.hills: The route is mostly flat, with only bridge and kerb gradients.
before_you_go.steps: No steps are required on the intended outdoor route.
before_you_go.accessibility: Checkpoints are on public routes, but busy crossings, riverside works and ordinary kerbs may affect access.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current council and Priory Centre facility information before setting off; opening arrangements can change.
before_you_go.footwear: Everyday walking shoes should be suitable, with extra grip useful after rain near the river.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally suitable using the main pavements and dropped kerbs.

recommended_age: Recommended 8+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A very compact town-centre loop linking the market area, river and public riverside paths.
